DIS.rationale: Disney presents a moderately attractive setup anchored by stable operating income ($4.60B in Q2 FY2026, flat YoY) and a near-trough P/E of 14.3x versus 23.5x a year ago — a 39% multiple compression that appears to overstate operating-business deterioration. The core franchise is genuinely strong: Experiences generated record $10B operating income in FY2025, streaming inflected to profitability ($1.3B FY2025 OI, 88% YoY growth to $582M in Q2 FY2026 with SVOD margin crossing 10%), and the IP flywheel has no true peer. The key concern is the persistent below-the-line drag compressing net income (-27.5% YoY despite flat operating income), which the market is pricing as if it were operating weakness. Balance sheet is adequate (0.78x D/E, equity $115.3B vs liabilities $89.9B) and cash generation is healthy ($6.91B OCF in Q2). Regulatory headwinds (FCC license review, European patent injunction, antitrust settlement) are material but do not impair the core flywheel. The Q3 FY2026 earnings call on August 5, 2026 provides a near-term catalyst: if net income narrows the gap to operating income, confirming earnings stabilization, re-rating potential is meaningful (conservative 16-17x on ~$1.30 EPS implies 20-25% upside). Score of +0.35 reflects good fundamentals and trajectory at a clearly depressed valuation, with a modest catalyst bump, tempered by below-the-line earnings uncertainty and regulatory overhang.
key_factors: Operating income stable at $4.60B in Q2 FY2026, flat YoY vs $4.44B — core business not deteriorating

P/E of 14.3x is near the 365-day trough (12.5x-23.6x range) and down 39% from 23.5x a year ago — market pricing net-income weakness as operating weakness
Experiences segment: record $10.0B operating income in FY2025, the structural profit engine
Streaming inflected: $1.3B operating income in FY2025, Q2 FY2026 OI up 88% to $582M, SVOD margin crossed 10% for first time, 196M subscribers
Operating cash flow $6.91B in Q2 FY2026 (+2.4% YoY), healthy cash generation
Balance sheet: equity $115.3B, D/E 0.78x (total liabilities/equity), manageable leverage
Q3 FY2026 earnings call August 5, 2026 — near-term catalyst for earnings stabilization confirmation
FCC regulatory standoff over ABC broadcast licenses (June 25, 2026) introduces reputational and operational uncertainty
European patent injunction on HEVC video encoding across 11 EU member states; $50M antitrust settlement on carriage practices
Linear TV structural decline remains a known headwind; $60B parks capex commitment over 10 years introduces execution risk
Analyst targets: Guggenheim $120, Rosenblatt $126, Raymond James $111 — all above current $99.71 price
